## Second independent agent misled by the same omission — raising to P2

Filed P3 as a discoverability gap. It has now demonstrably caused **two independent agents** to
reach the same false conclusion, so the cost is higher than 'someone has to look harder'.

### Occurrence 1 (coordinator, earlier today)

Read `rebar transition --help`, saw no `--caused-by`, concluded the flag did not exist, and filed a
**P1** asserting the documented remedy was inert. Also propagated the wrong conclusion into
instructions to four other agents. Withdrawn only after a peer session demonstrated the flag works
in a zero-commit store where blame could not have drawn the edge.

### Occurrence 2 (agent closing `evileyed-depletive-flycatcher`, minutes ago)

Independently reported, verbatim:

> **One correction to your instructions:** there is no `--caused-by` flag on `transition` in either
> the global or repo build — `rebar transition --help` lists only `--class`, `--reason`, `--force`,
> `--ref`, `--output`. `caused_by` is a **link relation** here, so I recorded it via `rebar link`.

Same source, same inference, same wrong answer — reached by an agent that had no contact with
occurrence 1. Two independent hits is the signal: a reader doing the reasonable thing (consult
`--help`) is reliably misled.

### Why the cost is real, not cosmetic

The `/rebar-debug` protocol makes passing `--caused-by` on a bug close **mandatory**, on the grounds
that an empty flag re-runs blame auto-derivation and can attach a WRONG origin — a worse input to
the escape-rate metric than no edge at all. An agent that concludes the flag does not exist will
close bare and let blame guess, which is exactly the failure the instruction exists to prevent.

In occurrence 2 the outcome was fine only because that agent independently recorded the edge with
`rebar link`. That was good judgement, not a property of the system.

### What this does NOT change

The 8,000-char limit, the parser, and the flag all work. `_parse_flags`
(`_commands/transition.py:123-124,164`) registers and returns it, and
`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_caused_by_autoderive.py:33` drives it through the CLI and passes.
The defect remains exactly what this ticket says: `_cli/help/transition.txt` and the help blob at
`_commands/transition.py:65` are two sources that drifted when `0f999860ad` updated only the latter.

The acceptance criteria already require fixing the duplication at the root rather than copying the
line across — that requirement is unchanged and is the right one. Only the priority moves.
